prompt: On one straight stretch of highway, mile marker $B$ sits between markers $A$ and $C$. Which pair below are opposite rays?
hint: Opposite rays must start at the SAME point and head in exactly opposite directions.

hints.text: Opposite rays must start at the SAME point and head in exactly opposite directions.
In ray notation the first letter is the starting point. Which choice has both rays starting at $B$?
$\overrightarrow{BA}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}$ both start at $B$ and point opposite ways along the highway.

explanation: Opposite rays share an endpoint and together form a straight line.
The first letter of a ray names its endpoint, so both rays must begin with $B$.
$\overrightarrow{BA}$ heads one way down the highway and $\overrightarrow{BC}$ heads the other: they are opposite rays.

alternativeExplanations.title: Stand at the marker
steps: Stand on marker $B$ and face $A$ — that is $\overrightarrow{BA}$.
Now turn all the way around and face $C$ — that is $\overrightarrow{BC}$. Same feet, opposite directions.
